reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure,let mu be any probability measure on E,and let eta be any real number with eta>0. Put d=dim_R E,allowing d=0,and define the actual scalar and real-valued function
  C=((sqrt(2 pi eta))^(-1))^d,
  Z(y)=integral_E exp(-||y-x||^2/(2 eta)) dmu(x).
The integral is the real Bochner integral. Let G be the standard centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure on E,and let volume be canonical Lebesgue measure on this inner-product space. Then the following four conclusions hold simultaneously:
  (mu x G)_*( (x,g) -> x+sqrt(eta)g )
    = volume.withDensity(y -> ENNReal.ofReal(C Z(y)));
  C Z(y)>0 for every y in E;
  Z:E->R is globally twice continuously Frechet differentiable;
  y -> -log(C Z(y)) is globally twice continuously Frechet differentiable.
The product mu x G is independent,and the pushforward is the law of X+sqrt(eta)G when X has law mu and the Gaussian vector is independent of X. The right side is the actual Lebesgue-density measure using the displayed normalizer and convolution integral. The positivity conclusion holds everywhere,not merely almost everywhere,and the negative-log function is defined from that exact normalized density. Real exponential,logarithm and square root have the stated real meanings.
No density,absolute continuity or finite-moment assumption is imposed on the input probability measure mu. There is no upper bound or small-step assumption on eta and no exclusion of zero dimension. The theorem asserts the exact measure equality,pointwise positive density and the two global C2 statements;it does not assert higher smoothness,analyticity,convexity,Hessian bounds,gradient Lipschitz constants,a diffusion evolution or a sampling algorithm.
objects: Finite-dimensional real-inner-product Borel space E;arbitrary probability measure mu;strictly positive real eta;finite real dimension d;actual Gaussian normalizer C;real convolution integral Z;standard centered identity-covariance Gaussian G;independent product law,pushforward under (x,g)->x+sqrt(eta)g;canonical Lebesgue volume;actual density C Z and its exact negative logarithm.
domains: E is finite-dimensional real-inner-product with its Borel measurable structure. mu is Measure E with IsProbabilityMeasure;eta in R with eta>0;d=Module.finrank R E in N and may be zero. C in R;Z:E->R. G and volume are measures on E;the independent product law lies on E x E and its pushforward lies on E. Density is embedded into ENNReal via ofReal;Z and negative-log density are real-valued functions on all E. Norm is induced by the given inner product. No separately supplied input density or vector-valued potential appears.
quantifiers: For every E with the stated structures,every probability mu on E,and every eta>0,define exactly C and Z;then the four displayed conclusions hold simultaneously. Density positivity is for every y in E. Both ContDiff R 2 conclusions are global over all E. The measure equality identifies the full measures,not only values on a selected set or almost-everywhere representatives. C and Z are fixed definitions,not existentially selected functions.
assumptions: Only the finite-dimensional real-inner-product/Borel structure,the probability normalization of mu,and eta>0. No finite moment,input Lebesgue density,absolute continuity,regularity of mu,eta upper bound,nonzero dimension,integrability certificate or supplied smoothness/density identity is assumed. The approved definitions specify the real Bochner integral,standard Gaussian,canonical volume and density measure.
conclusion: The pushforward of mu.prod G under (x,g)->x+sqrt(eta)g equals volume.withDensity(ofReal(C Z)). For every y,C Z(y)>0. Z is globally ContDiff R 2,and the actual function y->-Real.log(C Z(y)) is globally ContDiff R 2. These four assertions are simultaneous and use the displayed exact C,Z.
scopes: Measure equality concerns the actual independent-noise pushforward and the actual volume-density measure. Positivity is everywhere;the negative logarithm uses exactly that normalized density. The smoothness conclusions are C2,not an asserted C-infinity or analytic result. The input mu is unrestricted apart from being a probability measure,so no input density or finite-moment condition is added. Dimension zero is permitted. No Hessian,convexity,gradient bound,diffusion semigroup or numerical algorithm is asserted. No material ambiguity or definition gap is present.
constant_dependencies: Exact normalizer C=((sqrt(2*pi*eta))^(-1))^d with natural exponent d=finrank_R E. Exact kernel exponent -||y-x||^2/(2*eta),and noise scale sqrt(eta). The logarithm is -log(C Z(y)) including the normalizer,not -log Z alone. C depends only on eta,d;Z depends on eta,mu and y. There is no omitted volume factor,unspecified constant,moment parameter or smoothness-bound coefficient.
